synopsis: MAVS is an open-source university off-road simulation library associated with Mississippi State University and, in military/general off-road examples, ERDC [f15935, f3740, f4508, f4159]. It procedurally generates terrain with controllable roughness, ecosystem, haze and moonlight, provides automatic scene labels, and offers ray-traced lidar, camera and radar interacting with rain, dust, fog and snow [f3786, f3975, f4508]. Its tire-soil model is validated for sand and clay; dense-vegetation lidar validation was qualitative in 2018, and a field-measurement-based vegetation-override resistance model was reported at GVSETS 2025 [f3965, f4160, f3967]. Validation remains qualified: the 2020 paper described ongoing validation, and cited open-source simulator authors identified real-sensor validation as future work, despite claims of validated individual MAVS models [f4509, f3741, f3740]. A 2023 MAVS-based ecosystem study found changed segmentation results outside the training distribution, while a 2023 simulated-versus-real RELLIS-3D comparison found large domain-shift effects; MAVS frame rates were not found in the corpus [f4098, f4741, f4957].
